title: tenant SLA label mispropagation causes burst routing to cold pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A high-severity customer escalation: recent traffic spikes for multiple customers resulted in requests being routed to cold dedicated pools instead of their reserved warm pools. This caused increased cold starts, token-level latency regression, and token throttling for tiered SLA customers. We observed this behavior after a control-plane rollout that introduced a metadata propagation optimization for tenant SLA labels.
environment: production (us-west-2, eu-west-1); Dedicated reserved pools + control plane label propagation service
impact: Affected 6 enterprise tenants (P1/P0 SLAs). Observed 6-12x increase in token latency during bursts, ~18% error spike for requests hitting cold pools, billing-sensitive customers reported degraded SLAs. Customer escalations opened with support and SRE teams.

reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy control-plane label optimization (async write path) to a canary region
2) Create tenant with reserved pool and SLA tier 'gold'
3) Simulate burst traffic (sustained 200 RPS for tenant) while toggling control-plane leader failover
4) Observe router logs for routing decision when 'sla_tier' metadata is missing or stale
5) Verify requests are routed to default cold pool instead of tenant's reserved pool
root_cause: An optimization changed SLA label writes to an async, unordered path that batched label mutations. Under certain timing (concurrent leader re-election or cache invalidation) the router's read path observed a TTL-expired or missing 'sla_tier' key and fell back to default routing. This created a window where bursts were sent to cold capacity. The control-plane change lacked a read-after-write guarantee for tenant SLA labels and no end-to-end tests covered leader failover paths.
mitigation: Immediate: Rollback control-plane optimization v12.3.1 -> v12.3.0 in all regions (completed 2025-02-18)
Short-term: Add guard in router to consult recent write-ahead log if SLA label missing; route using last-known-good mapping for 30s
Medium-term: Deploy deterministic ordered write path for SLA labels with read-after-write consistency (PR #3782 merged to main) and canary rollout
Monitoring: Add metric 'routing.sla_label_miss_rate' and alert if >0.1% over 5m for a region
Customer support: Send targeted incident comms to affected tenants and credit uplift where SLA breached
fix_notes: PR #3782 enforces ordered writes and retries on writer leader changes. Additional unit tests simulate leader failover during label commit. Integration tests added to the canary pipeline to simulate rapid leader re-election combined with metadata reads. Router fallback implemented as soft-guard prior to full rollout.
customer_communications: ACME Health: initial acknowledgment sent 2025-02-18 02:40 UTC; follow-up with mitigation and credits on 2025-02-22
BeaconPay: informed 2025-02-19 about rollback and canary plan; scheduled technical deep-dive 2025-02-25
postmortem_summary: A control-plane optimization introduced an async write path for tenant SLA labels which under rare leader re-election timing could be observed as missing by the router, leading to incorrect fallback routing to cold pools during bursts. Primary contributing factors: lack of read-after-write guarantee, insufficient integration tests for leader failover scenarios, and inadequate observability on SLA label propagation. Immediate rollback and router guards mitigated impact; ordered writes and better testing prevent recurrence.
